description: What is the basic accounting equation?
explanation: The accounting equation Assets = Liabilities + Equity is the foundation of double-entry bookkeeping. Every transaction keeps this equation in balance.

description: A debit entry increases which type of account?
explanation: Debits increase asset and expense accounts and decrease liability and equity accounts. This is a fundamental rule of double-entry bookkeeping.

description: What does GAAP stand for?
explanation: GAAP stands for Generally Accepted Accounting Principles. These are the standard rules and guidelines that U.S. companies must follow when preparing financial statements.

description: Which financial statement shows a company's financial position at a specific point in time?
explanation: The balance sheet (also called the statement of financial position) shows assets
calculator: and equity at a single date. The income statement and cash flow statement cover a period of time.

description: A credit entry increases which type of account?
explanation: Credits increase liability
calculator: and revenue accounts. Credits decrease asset and expense accounts. This is the opposite of how debits work.

description: Which of the following is a current asset?
explanation: Current assets are assets expected to be converted to cash within one year. Accounts receivable is a current asset. Land and equipment are long-term assets. Common stock is an equity item.

description: If a company has assets of $100000 and liabilities of $60000
explanation: what is the owners equity?

description: Which of the following appears on the income statement?
explanation: The income statement reports revenues and expenses over a period of time to calculate net income. Accounts payable and cash are balance sheet items. Retained earnings is an equity account.

description: What type of account is Accounts Payable?
explanation: Accounts Payable represents money owed to suppliers. It is a liability because it is an obligation the company must pay in the future.

description: The principle that states revenue should be recorded when earned is called?
explanation: The revenue recognition principle states that revenue is recorded when it is earned
hint: not necessarily when cash is received. This is a core component of accrual-basis accounting.

description: Which financial statement reports revenues and expenses?
explanation: The income statement (also called profit and loss statement) reports all revenues earned and expenses incurred during an accounting period
hint: resulting in net income or net loss.

description: Which of the following is a long-term liability?
explanation: Bonds payable are long-term obligations due beyond one year. Accounts payable
calculator: and unearned revenue are typically current liabilities due within one year.

description: To record a cash sale
explanation: you would debit which account?
calculator: you debit Cash (an asset account increases) and credit Revenue. Debits increase assets.

description: Which of the following would increase total assets?
explanation: Borrowing money from a bank increases Cash (an asset) and also increases Notes Payable (a liability)
hint: so total assets increase. Paying off debt reduces both assets and liabilities.

description: The going concern assumption means that?
explanation: The going concern assumption holds that a business will continue to operate for the foreseeable future. This justifies recording long-term assets at cost rather than liquidation value.
choice0: The company must earn a profit
choice1: The company will pay all debts immediately
choice2: The company is about to close
choice3: The company will continue operating in the future

description: Net income from the income statement flows into which other financial statement?
explanation: Net income increases retained earnings
hint: which is reported on the statement of retained earnings and ultimately on the balance sheet under equity. It also appears in the operating section of the cash flow statement (indirect method).

description: Which of the following is an example of an expense account?
explanation: Wages Expense is an expense account that increases with a debit. Cash and Prepaid Insurance are asset accounts. Common Stock is an equity account.

description: Assets on a balance sheet are listed in order of?
explanation: Assets are listed on the balance sheet in order of liquidity - how quickly they can be converted to cash. Cash is listed first

description: Owner investments into a business increase which two elements of the accounting equation?
explanation: When an owner invests cash into a business
hint: assets (cash) increase and equity (common stock or owner capital) increases. Liabilities are not affected.

description: Gross profit is calculated as?
explanation: Gross profit equals net sales minus cost of goods sold. It measures how efficiently a company produces or purchases goods relative to the revenue those goods generate.
choice1: Net Sales - Cost of Goods Sold

description: What is a journal entry?
explanation: A journal entry is the recording of a business transaction in the accounting books using the double-entry system. Every entry has at least one debit and one credit that must equal each other.
choice2: A record of a transaction with debits and credits
choice3: A list of all accounts in the ledger

description: The cost principle states that assets should be recorded at?
explanation: The cost principle (historical cost principle) requires that assets be recorded at their original purchase price
hint: not their current market value. This provides objectivity and verifiability.

description: Under cash basis accounting
explanation: revenue is recorded when?
calculator: revenue is recognized only when cash is actually received
verified: not when the service is performed or product delivered. This differs from accrual accounting.

description: What are the three main sections of a balance sheet?
explanation: A balance sheet is divided into assets
calculator: and equity (also called owners equity or stockholders equity). These three sections must always be in balance.

description: Which account has a normal credit balance?
explanation: Revenue accounts have a normal credit balance because credits increase revenue. Assets and expenses have normal debit balances. Revenues and liabilities have normal credit balances.

description: The cash flow statement is divided into which three sections?
explanation: The statement of cash flows has three sections: operating activities (day-to-day business)
calculator: and financing activities (borrowing and repaying debt or issuing stock).

description: When a company pays rent in cash
explanation: which accounts are affected?
hint: Paying rent in cash is an expense. Rent Expense is debited (increases the expense) and Cash is credited (decreases the asset). This keeps the accounting equation in balance.

description: Accounts Receivable represents?
explanation: Accounts Receivable is a current asset representing money owed to the company by customers who purchased goods or services on credit. It is expected to be collected within the normal operating cycle.
choice1: Money owed to the company by customers

description: The matching principle requires that?
explanation: The matching principle states that expenses should be recorded in the same period as the revenues they helped generate. This ensures that net income accurately reflects the cost of earning that revenue.
choice0: Assets must equal liabilities plus equity
choice2: Expenses are recorded in the same period as related revenues
choice3: All transactions must be recorded immediately

description: Which of the following would appear under stockholders equity on a balance sheet?
explanation: Retained Earnings is a component of stockholders equity representing accumulated net income not paid as dividends. Accounts payable is a liability. Cash and inventory are assets.

description: Operating expenses are subtracted from gross profit to arrive at?
explanation: After subtracting operating expenses (such as salaries
verified: the result is operating income (also called income from operations or operating profit).

description: Which transaction would decrease both assets and liabilities?
explanation: Paying off accounts payable with cash decreases Cash (an asset) and decreases Accounts Payable (a liability). The accounting equation remains balanced.

description: The general ledger is?
explanation: The general ledger is a complete record of all accounts and their balances. It contains individual accounts for assets
point: with all debit and credit entries posted to them.
column17: A daily record of cash received
column18: A complete record of all accounts and their balances
column19: A summary of the income statement

description: When supplies are purchased on credit
explanation: the journal entry is?
hint: Purchasing supplies on credit means you receive supplies (asset increases - debit Supplies) and owe money to the supplier (liability increases - credit Accounts Payable).

description: Which statement shows cash generated from business operations?
explanation: The cash flow statement's operating activities section shows cash inflows and outflows from the core business operations - collecting from customers

explanation: accounts payable?

description: The principle of conservatism in accounting means?
explanation: The conservatism principle (prudence) means that when in doubt
hint: accountants should choose the option that results in lower net income or lower asset values. This avoids overstating financial health.
choice1: Always choose the most profitable option
choice2: Record revenue as early as possible
column15: choose the option that is least likely to overstate assets or income

description: Prepaid insurance is classified as?
explanation: Prepaid insurance is a current asset because it represents a future economic benefit (insurance coverage) that has already been paid for but not yet used. It will be expensed as the coverage period passes.

description: Which of the following is NOT typically an operating expense?
explanation: Interest expense is a non-operating (financial) expense. Rent
calculator: and salaries are all typical operating expenses related to running the core business.

description: Dividends paid to shareholders affect which part of the accounting equation?
explanation: Dividends reduce Retained Earnings
hint: which is a component of Equity. They also reduce Cash (an asset). Dividends are not expenses on the income statement.

description: The chart of accounts is?
explanation: The chart of accounts is a numbered list of all accounts used by a business. It organizes accounts into categories (assets
correct: expenses) and assigns each a unique number for easy reference.
column15: A record of daily cash transactions
column16: A list of all outstanding customer invoices
column17: A complete list of all accounts used in the accounting system
column18: A report comparing budget to actual

description: Under accrual accounting
explanation: expenses are recorded when?
calculator: expenses are recognized when they are incurred (when the benefit is received)
verified: not when cash is actually paid. This matches expenses to the period in which they help generate revenue.

description: When a customer pays their outstanding balance
explanation: which accounts are affected?
hint: When a customer pays their account
calculator: Cash increases (debit Cash) and the amount they owe you decreases (credit Accounts Receivable). Revenue was already recorded when the sale was made.

description: Which section of the balance sheet lists resources owned by the company?
explanation: The assets section of the balance sheet lists all resources owned or controlled by the company that have future economic value. Assets are typically listed in order of liquidity.

description: The entity concept means?
explanation: The entity concept (or economic entity assumption) requires that the business be treated as separate from its owners for accounting purposes. Personal transactions of the owner must not be mixed with business transactions.
choice1: A business must pay all taxes on time
choice2: Business transactions are kept separate from personal transactions
choice3: A company can only have one owner

description: Notes Payable is classified as?
explanation: Notes Payable is a liability because it represents a formal written promise to repay borrowed money. If due within one year it is a current liability; if due beyond one year it is a long-term liability.

description: What does net income represent?
explanation: Net income (also called the bottom line) is the amount remaining after all revenues have been recognized and all expenses have been deducted during an accounting period. It increases retained earnings.

description: The allowance for doubtful accounts is?
explanation: The allowance for doubtful accounts is a contra-asset account used to estimate the portion of accounts receivable that will not be collected. It reduces the net realizable value of accounts receivable on the balance sheet.
choice0: An amount set aside for future purchases
choice1: A contra-asset account estimating uncollectible receivables

description: When a company borrows money from a bank by signing a note payable
explanation: the journal entry includes?
hint: Borrowing cash from a bank increases your Cash (asset - debit) and creates an obligation to repay (Notes Payable - liability increases with a credit).

description: Unearned revenue is classified as?
explanation: Unearned revenue (also called deferred revenue) is a liability because the company has received cash but has not yet performed the service or delivered the product. The company owes the customer the goods or service.
